at.description: Absolute target: an RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a local date, time, and IANA time_zone.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send one durable message to another Team member. A running target receives it at the nearest step boundary; an inactive target starts or resumes a turn.

target.description: Member target returned by spawn_teammate or list_agents, including lead.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: spawn_teammate
tools.description: Create one named, durable teammate. Only the Team Lead may call this tool.

description.description: Short description of the delegated responsibility.

prompt.description: Complete initial task for the teammate.

context.description: fresh starts without Lead history; fork inherits completed Lead turns. Defaults to fresh.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles. Child LLM selection is optional. Omit `provider`, `model`, and `reasoning_effort` to use configured child defaults and inherit compatible missing values from the parent Agent. Supply `provider` and `model` together after using `list_subagent_models` to inspect advertised routes and efforts. Changing the effective route without naming an effort uses the selected model's default effort.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

provider.description: LLM provider route for the child. Supply together with model; omit both to use configured child defaults or inherit the parent route.

model.description: Model id interpreted by provider. Supply together with provider; omit both to use configured child defaults or inherit the parent route.

reasoning_effort.description: Adapter-owned reasoning effort for the effective child route. Omit to inherit a compatible configured/parent effort or use a newly selected model's default.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true. Set false only when your next action depends on the result.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true. Set false only when your next action depends on the result.

tools.name: task_board_create
tools.description: Create a task on the DSH task board, or a subtask by passing parentId. A subtask inherits every execution target it does not override (workspace, agent preset, permission, model) from its parent, and inherits the parent human permission confirmation together with an inherited binding. The deployment caps subtask depth (default one level, maximum three): a subtask of a subtask is refused unless the board is configured deeper. The task lands in the todo column and does NOT run; call task_board_run to execute it. Triggers: 任务看板, task board, 看板, 新建任务, create task, 子任务, subtask, 定时任务.

description.description: Longer human description shown in the detail view.

prompt.description: The instruction sent to the execution agent; the title is used when blank.

parentId.description: Parent task id, making this a subtask. Omit for a root task.

workspaceId.description: Workspace id the execution must run in; omit to inherit the parent value or use the most recent workspace.

mode.description: Agent preset id the execution session is composed from; omit for the deployment default or the parent value.

permission.description: Permission preset for the execution session. Omit to inherit the parent binding; a value above the session default needs a human confirmation in the board UI before the card can run.

model.description: Pinned model as provider/model (or a model id); omit for the host default or the parent value.

reuseSession.description: Continue later runs in the previous execution session instead of a fresh conversation.

teamRun.description: Run this task as an Agent Team: running it starts one Team Lead session and the Host spawns a teammate per subtask inside it. Omit or false for one independent session per member. Refused when the deployment serves no Agent Teams service.

goalRun.description: Start each run with dsh built-in /goal so the session keeps working continuation rounds until the goal completes. Default true (omit to keep it); pass false for a single plain turn.

tags.description: Labels: the name renders as a badge and drives the board filter; promptPrefix is injected ahead of the execution prompt on every run.

name.description: Label name (unique within the task, at most 32 characters).

promptPrefix.description: Optional prompt line injected before the task prompt (at most 200 characters).

schedule.description: Arm a 5-field cron schedule at creation time (Host local time zone).

cron.description: 5-field cron: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week.

tools.name: task_board_get
tools.description: Read one task board card in full: prompt, description, labels, column, parent link, direct subtasks, execution targets, schedule, permission gate state, and the last ten execution attempts with their session ids and outcomes. Use it before running or editing a card, and after a run to read the settled outcome. Triggers: 任务看板, task board, 看板, 子任务, subtask, task detail.

taskId.description: Task id, as reported by task_board_list or task_board_create.

tools.name: task_board_list
tools.description: List tasks on the DSH task board (the Host-authoritative ledger behind the Web GUI task board). Filters: status column, parentId (direct subtasks), rootsOnly, tag, free-text query, and archived inclusion. Returns each task id, title, column, parent/subtask link, execution targets, schedule and latest run outcome, plus the board summary (revision, time zone, subtask depth limit, session-default permission). Use task_board_get for one task in full, task_board_create to add work, and task_board_run to execute it. Triggers: 任务看板, task board, 看板, 子任务, subtask, task list, 定时任务, scheduled task.

parentId.description: Only the direct subtasks of this task id.

rootsOnly.description: Only tasks that have no parent (default false).

tag.description: Only tasks carrying this label name.

query.description: Case-insensitive match against title, description, prompt, and label names.

tools.name: task_board_manage
tools.description: Move, archive, restore, delete, or settle one task board card. move-todo and move-backlog are the manual column moves; a running card cannot be moved. settle force-closes the open execution of a card the board can no longer observe (a stuck running card) and records it cancelled with the caller as the reason, so the card returns to the todo column and can be run again. archive takes the whole subtask tree off the board and is refused while any member has an unsettled execution; restore brings the task, its ancestors and its subtree back; delete removes one card and is refused while it still has subtasks (detach or delete them first) or while it runs. It cannot confirm a permission binding: the confirmation gate is a human act performed in the board UI. Triggers: 任务看板, task board, 看板, 归档, archive, 删除任务, delete task, 移动任务, move task, 卡住, stuck, 强制结算, settle.

tools.name: task_board_run
tools.description: Run a task on the board now, or re-run a settled one. Running a task also runs its whole subtask tree CONCURRENTLY: the Host opens one real DSH session per member under one run group, each replaying its card pinned workspace, agent preset, permission and model; a subtask that does not pin them inherits its nearest ancestor. The parent card stays in the running column until its own turn and every direct subtask have settled, and it fails when any member failed; one failing subtask never stops the others. A card whose effective permission is above the deployment session default is refused with confirmation-required until a HUMAN confirms the binding in the board UI; this tool cannot confirm it. A card whose task carries teamRun instead starts ONE Team Lead session and the Host spawns a teammate per subtask inside it, so those cards run as an Agent Team rather than as independent sessions; that mode needs the deployment Agent Teams service and is refused when it is missing. Executions consume real API quota. Sessions are created asynchronously, so read their ids and outcomes back with task_board_get. Triggers: 任务看板, task board, 看板, 执行任务, run task, 重新执行, rerun, 子任务, subtask.

taskId.description: The task to run; running a root task runs its whole subtree.

rerun.description: Re-run a settled task: reset its column to todo before starting (default false).

tools.name: task_board_schedule
tools.description: Arm, change, or disarm a task scheduled runs (5-field cron; day-of-month and day-of-week follow Vixie semantics: both restricted means OR, otherwise AND). The cron wall clock is read in the rule stored IANA time zone; omit timeZone to use the Host zone reported by task_board_list/task_board_get. DST gaps are skipped and an ambiguous fall-back time fires once, at the earlier instant. A due scheduled task runs the same cascade a manual run does, so a root task runs its whole subtask tree. A schedule whose tree contains an unconfirmed above-default permission is refused and rolls to its next occurrence; the reason is reported in the list board summary as schedulerError. Missed occurrences during Host downtime are skipped, never queued; a task that is already running skips its occurrence. Triggers: 任务看板, task board, 看板, 定时任务, schedule, cron, 每天执行.

cron.description: 5-field cron expression: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week.

timeZone.description: IANA zone the cron wall clock is read in (for example Asia/Shanghai). Omit to keep the stored zone, or pass an empty string to clear it back to the Host zone.

tools.name: task_board_set_parent
tools.description: Attach an existing task under a parent (making it a subtask) or detach it back to the root board by setting its parentId. Pass an empty parentId to detach. The Host refuses the link when the parent is unknown or archived, when the moved task is one of its own descendants, when the resulting depth exceeds the deployment subtask limit (default one level, maximum three), or while the task has an unsettled execution (its link may still be a running cascade parent pointer). Running a task runs its whole subtree concurrently; a parent card settles only after its own turn and every direct subtask settle. Triggers: 任务看板, task board, 看板, 子任务, subtask, 关联任务, link task, 解除关联, detach.

taskId.description: The task whose parent link changes.

parentId.description: Parent task id, or an empty string to detach the task back to the root board.

tools.name: task_board_update
tools.description: Edit a task board card: title, description, prompt, labels, and the execution targets (workspace, agent preset, permission, model, session reuse). Only the fields you pass change; pass an empty string to clear a target, or an empty labels array to clear the labels. Title, description and prompt freeze once the task has started executing; the execution targets stay editable because they only affect future runs. Changing the pinned permission re-arms the permission confirmation gate. Triggers: 任务看板, task board, 看板, 修改任务, edit task, 子任务, 标签, tags.

title.description: New title (a blank title is refused by the Host).

description.description: New description.

workspaceId.description: New workspace id; an empty string clears it.

mode.description: New agent preset id; an empty string clears it.

permission.description: New permission preset; an empty string clears it back to the session default.

model.description: New pinned model; an empty string clears it.

reuseSession.description: Continue later runs in the previous execution session.

teamRun.description: Switches this task between a plain cascade (one session per member) and an Agent Team run (Lead session plus a teammate per subtask).

goalRun.description: Whether each run starts with dsh built-in /goal (default true). Pass false to run one plain turn instead.

tags.description: Replacement label set; an empty array clears all labels.

promptPrefix.description: Optional prompt line injected before the task prompt.

tools.name: team_task_create
tools.description: Create one unowned pending task on the shared Team task board.

description.description: Complete task details and acceptance criteria.

blocked_by.description: Task ids that must complete first.

write_scopes.description: Advisory workspace-relative file or directory prefixes this task expects to modify.

tools.name: team_task_get
tools.description: Read the complete latest value of one shared task before changing or executing it.

tools.name: team_task_list
tools.description: List shared tasks, including readiness, owner, revision, blockers, and write-scope warnings.

owner.description: Optional member target from spawn_teammate or list_agents, matching ownerName; use unowned for tasks without an owner.

limit.description: Number of rows, 1 through 100. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: team_task_update
tools.description: Compare-and-set a shared task action using the latest revision from team_task_get or team_task_list.

expected_revision.description: Current task revision used as the CAS precondition.

description.description: Replacement details for edit.

write_scopes.description: Replacement advisory write scopes for edit.

owner.description: Member target from spawn_teammate or list_agents for Lead-only reassign; omit to unassign.

tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

<skill_instructions>
# Long Task Continuation

## Overview

Keep long work checkpointed, resumable, drift-aware, and evidence-gated. This
protocol does not execute plans, dispatch subagents, run tests, or grant
completion authority.

## Authority Boundary

The Method Pack owns continuation discipline only. It does not own the parent
plan, host retry/watchdog behavior, authoritative `GateDecision`, evidence
sufficiency, requirement acceptance, or completion.

## When To Use

Use this skill when the work has meaningful phases, may be compacted/resumed or
handed off, uses subagents, or explicitly needs continuity and drift control.
Architecture, contract, shared-workflow, and verification-gate changes also
benefit from it. Do not force it onto a short answer or one-command check.

Choose exactly one state carrier:

- use a durable `work/` record for medium+ work that actually crosses sessions,
  needs handoff, or requires resumable state;
- otherwise keep one inline checkpoint.

Multi-step, todo-driven, possible-compaction, and subagent use do not force
durable records by themselves. Do not create both carriers or a record per
slice.

## Required Artifacts

A durable task has one process trail under
`docs/aegis/work/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/`. It keeps logical intent/baseline state,
the latest todo/checkpoint/resume state, terminal evidence/drift state, and a
completion reflection when warranted. These are
`TaskIntentDraft`, `BaselineReadSetHint`, `BaselineUsageDraft`,
`ImpactStatementDraft`, `TodoCheckpointDraft`, `ResumeStateHint`,
`DriftCheckDraft`, and `EvidenceBundleDraft` views—not authoritative runtime
records or separate plan owners.

Read only the lifecycle-matched section of `durable-work-guidance.md`:

- `## Required Artifact Layout` and `## Create A Durable Work Record` for a new durable work record;
- `## Update A Slice` when an existing helper-backed record needs sidecar updates;
- `## Retry Convergence Detail` for retry/attempt bookkeeping;
- `## Pause, Handoff, And Completion Bundle` when preparing a pause, handoff, or completion bundle; and
- `## Expanded State Fields` only when natural checkpoint prose is ambiguous.

The reference owns artifact layout and `<aegis-workspace-helper>` command
detail; this file owns carrier selection, resume order, drift decisions, and
stop conditions.

An `Execution Readiness View` may be kept in the intent or active checkpoint
for medium/high, handoff-prone, long-running, subagent-driven, architecture,
contract, compatibility, or retirement-sensitive work. It renders existing
intent, scope, baseline, owner, test, review, and drift constraints; it is not a
new JSON artifact or completion authority.

Planless Slice Lane:

- When an existing parent plan/spec owns a bounded task, reuse it and the
  current checkpoint. For a no-parent direct bounded request with no new
  durable or unclear verification boundary, use an inline checkpoint.
- State one compact `Slice Card`: Goal, `Parent plan/spec` (or
  `none — direct bounded request`), Files, Boundary, Verification, and Stop.
- The slice goal closes only that slice. Final completion returns to the parent
  or direct bounded request through `verification-before-completion`.
- Do not create a plan/spec merely to give a micro-slice a parent, and do not
  create per-slice plans/specs or work records.
- Escalate when a new owner, contract, schema, public API, architecture,
  migration, persistence, security/permission, distribution/release surface,
  unclear verification boundary, or mismatch with parent scope or acceptance
  appears.

When durable architecture decisions are in scope, these work records are the
preferred ADR Auto Backfill source. Preserve decision signals, source refs,
alternatives, compatibility, retirement, drift, and baseline-sync questions.

## Start Protocol

Before execution:

1. Capture requested outcome, scope, non-goals, risks, parent plan/goal, success
   evidence, and stop states (`done | blocked | needs-verification |
   scope-exceeded`).
2. Identify required baseline refs and record acknowledged, cited, and missing
   refs. Missing authority pauses in `needs-baseline-readback`.
3. Choose inline or durable state once, then record the todo map, active slice,
   completed slices/evidence, blockers, next step, and current branch/HEAD.
4. When an `Execution Readiness View` exists, retain its intent lock, scope
   fence, baseline lock, compatibility/retirement boundary, tests, reviews,
   evidence, and rewind rules.
5. For a new helper-backed record, use `durable-work-guidance.md` to create and
   structurally check it before implementation.

## Retry Convergence Protocol

A failed verification is another attempt in the current slice, not a new
slice. Keep failed-attempt telemetry out of terminal evidence and normal
commits. Only `evidence-finalized`, `blocked`, or `abandoned` is terminal.
When retry state reaches `process-artifact-pressure`, stop auto-retry and route
to `systematic-debugging` or `verification-before-completion`. Load the durable
reference only when the attempt/evidence commands or sidecar rules are needed.

## Per-Slice Protocol

Before each slice, state the current goal/todo, intended edits, explicit
non-edits, verification, and readiness alignment. A bounded parent-plan or
no-parent slice uses the compact Slice Card rather than a new plan/spec.

After each slice, update completed todos, evidence refs, newly used baseline
refs, blockers, next step, and drift decision. When an active helper-backed work record exists, read `durable-work-guidance.md` and update that same record;
never create another workstream for bookkeeping.

When patch-shape/ripple triage, an H-class finding, or a bounded compatibility
mitigation fired, a locally green result does not clear the direction. Retain
`PatchShape`, `CanonicalOwner`, `UpwardDrillSignal`, latest outcome, and one
bounded evidence ref; do not copy raw logs or full diffs. If no fresh evidence
exists, the state is `needs-verification` or `partial`.

## Resume Protocol

Resume in this order:

1. Read original intent, parent plan/goal, latest checkpoint and resume hint.
2. Re-read required baseline refs and relevant active `CONTEXT.md` language.
3. Read the `Execution Readiness View` when present.
4. Compare checkpoint branch/HEAD, completed commits, evidence refs, and claims
   with the current worktree.
   Treat inherited completion claims as unverified until the worktree confirms
   them. Correct contradictions in the checkpoint, disclose them in the final
   report, and do not republish stale claims as current.
   Preserve the claim's subject, scope and resume-time state; distinguish that
   from later repair and from historical execution you cannot verify. One
   accurate correction may cover related claims. The record must adopt it,
   without elsewhere denying it or assigning it to another scope. A reviewer's
   classification is contestable: if material disagreement remains unresolved
   after checking evidence, retain `needs-verification` without forcing assent.
   If evidence resolves it, retain the supported conclusion and verify normally.
5. Compare the active slice against intent lock, scope fence, baseline lock,
   compatibility/retirement boundary, tests, reviews, and non-goals.

worktree pauses execution. A semantic conflict routes to
`establishing-project-context`; an unplanned repair re-reads the retained
invariant, owner seam, patch shape, and causal topology, then route comparison to
`systematic-debugging`. A new carrier name alone does not prove a new direction. Never resume from memory alone.

Check original intent and stop condition, parent scope/acceptance, compatibility,
new owners/fallbacks/adapters/branches, retirement, evidence freshness, and any
readiness locks. Allowed decisions are `continue`, `pause-for-user`,
`needs-baseline-readback`, `needs-verification`, and `blocked`.

Never emit `gate-passed`, `completion-granted`, or `authoritatively-safe`.

## Completion Candidate Protocol

Before a completion claim:

1. Use `aegis:verification-before-completion`.

Generated packs are future-runtime inputs only. Method Pack output remains
verified evidence and advisory judgment, not authoritative completion.

Report naturally and omit empty structures. Keep these semantic slots visible:
`Aegis Visibility`; current todo/active/completed/next; baseline usage decision;
readiness state when present; fresh evidence; inherited-claim corrections when
a resumed record overstated its state; retry/convergence state when
relevant; drift decision; risk/unknown; and the next smallest safe action.

14: /// <summary>Ported from interface/contracts.js ESCALATION_RULES: capability + resource pattern → escalated risk.</summary>
15: public sealed record EscalationRule(
16:     string Name,
17:     AgentCapability Capability,
18:     Regex Pattern,
19:     ToolRiskLevel EscalatedRisk,
20:     bool RequireConfirmation,
21:     string Reason);

23: /// <summary>
24: /// Deterministic risk escalation (AGENTS.md §11, threat T13): certain resources and
25: /// capabilities carry a higher effective risk than their declared one. Ported from
26: /// the browser protocol reference (interface/contracts.js), stage 1 of Option A
27: /// (docs/INTERFACE-ANALYSIS.md).
28: /// </summary>
29: public static class ToolEscalation
30: {
31:     public static readonly EscalationRule[] Rules =
32:     [
33:         new EscalationRule(
34:             "security-configuration",
35:             AgentCapability.WriteFile,
36:             new Regex(@"(\.git[\\/]hooks([\\/].*)?$|nuget\.config$|Directory\.Build\.(props|targets)$|\.tolik([\\/].*)?$|policy\.json$|CODEOWNERS$)", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.Compiled),
37:             ToolRiskLevel.Destructive,
38:             RequireConfirmation: true,
39:             Reason: "modifying build, pipeline or authorization policy configuration"),
40:         new EscalationRule(
41:             "security-critical-source",
42:             AgentCapability.WriteFile,
43:             new Regex(@"(ProtocolContracts\.cs|CoreRuntime\.cs|AgentRuntime\.cs|AuthorizationEngine\.cs|AuthorizationPolicy\.cs|ToolEscalation\.cs|SecurityLogging\.cs|AuditWriter\.cs|DeviceChallengeVerifier\.cs)$", RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.Compiled),
44:             ToolRiskLevel.Critical,
45:             RequireConfirmation: true,
46:             Reason: "modifying TOLIK's own security-critical source can bypass authorization (T13)"),
47:         new EscalationRule(
48:             "codex-autonomy",
49:             AgentCapability.RunCodex,
50:             new Regex(".", RegexOptions.Compiled),
51:             ToolRiskLevel.Modify,
52:             RequireConfirmation: true,
53:             Reason: "a coding agent can modify the working tree without review of each edit"),
54:     ];
55: 
56:     /// <summary>Returns the effective risk and the first matching rule (declared risk is the floor).</summary>
57:     public static (ToolRiskLevel EffectiveRisk, EscalationRule? Applied) Evaluate(AgentCapability capability, string resource)
58:     {
59:         var effective = ToolRiskLevel.ReadOnly;
60:         foreach (var rule in Rules)
61:         {
62:             if (rule.Capability != capability) continue;
63:             if (!rule.Pattern.IsMatch(resource)) continue;
64:             if (rule.EscalatedRisk > effective) effective = rule.EscalatedRisk;
65:             return (effective, rule);
66:         }
67:         return (effective, null);
68:     }
69: }

92:     public static AuthorizationDecision Evaluate(AuthorizationRequest request)
93:     {
94:         var now = request.EvaluatedAt ?? DateTimeOffset.UtcNow;
95:         if (!request.PolicyAvailable || request.Principal is null || !request.SessionValid || !request.DeviceValid ||
96:             !request.AgentAuthorized || !request.TaskScopeValid || !request.CapabilityGranted ||
97:             string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.Principal.Role) ||
98:             !string.Equals(request.Principal.Role, "Owner", StringComparison.Ordinal) &&
99:             !string.Equals(request.Principal.Role, "AuthorizedUser", StringComparison.Ordinal) ||
100:             request.Risk == ToolRiskLevel.Critical && !request.MfaValid ||
101:             string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.Resource) || string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.AllowedResource) ||
102:             !string.Equals(request.Resource, request.AllowedResource, StringComparison.Ordinal) ||
103:             request.AuthorizationExpiresAt is { } authorizationExpiry && authorizationExpiry <= now ||
104:             request.ConfirmationConsumed ||
105:             request.ConfirmationExpiresAt is { } confirmationExpiry && confirmationExpiry <= now)
106:             return AuthorizationDecision.Deny;
107: 
108:         // Effective risk = max(declared, escalated): security-critical resources and
109:         // autonomous coding agents escalate beyond their declared level (T13).
110:         var effectiveRisk = request.Risk;
111:         var (escalatedRisk, _) = ToolEscalation.Evaluate(request.Capability, request.Resource);
112:         if (escalatedRisk > effectiveRisk) effectiveRisk = escalatedRisk;
113:

1. `SessionPrincipal(Guid UserId, Guid DeviceId, Guid SessionId, string Role)` — Role is a string ("Owner", "AuthorizedUser").
2. `IdentityRole` enum in Contracts: Guest, AuthorizedUser, Owner.
3. `ToolRiskLevel` enum: ReadOnly, LowRisk, Modify, Destructive, Critical.

5. `ToolEscalation` gives the risk *floor* (escalation). What's missing is the *ceiling* — a role-based maximum risk.

"Roles and authorization ceilings" likely means:
- Formalize roles (maybe a role table/map rather than magic strings — though minimal).
- Add a per-role authorization ceiling: the maximum ToolRiskLevel a role may be authorized for. E.g., Guest → nothing (deny all), AuthorizedUser → up to Destructive (no Critical), Owner → up to Critical (with MFA).
- Fail closed: if effective risk exceeds role ceiling → Deny (not ConfirmationRequired).

This prevents privilege escalation: even if a Guest/AuthorizedUser somehow obtains a valid confirmation for a Critical op, the ceiling denies it. 1: # TOLIK Security
2: 
3: ## Threat Model
4: 
5: TOLIK handles sensitive personal data:
6: - Private conversations
7: - Personal information
8: - Credentials and tokens
9: - Home environment data
10: - Computer access
11: 
12: ## Security Layers
13: 
14: ### 1. Identity
15: - Device identity verification
16: - Session-based authentication
17: - Bootstrap code for initial setup
18: - Challenge-response for revocation
19: - Speaker verification (CampPlus embedding, threshold 0.45): `POST /voice/speaker/enroll`
20:   stores a Private voice profile, `POST /voice/speaker/verify` returns confidence.
21:   Voice confidence alone never authorizes. Enforcement wired in `/voice/turn`:
22:   unverified speakers get a guest-mode instruction (no private items, no
23:   irreversible acts) + `voice.user.unverified` provenance; tool-level gating
24:   beyond that is future work.
25: 
26: ### 2. Authorization
27: - Per-tool capability system
28: - READ_ONLY / LOW_RISK / MODIFY / DESTRUCTIVE / CRITICAL
29: - Context-aware authorization
30: - Audit trail for all decisions
31: - Normative matrix: `docs/authorization.md` (categories, escalation rules,
32:   confirmation binding, MFA categories)
33: 
34: ### 3. Tool Security
35: - Explicit capability list per tool
36: - Path isolation (TOLIK_ALLOWED_ROOTS)
37: - Never unrestricted shell access
38: - Destructive operations require confirmation
39: - Agent disconnect is owner-authenticated; Core atomically removes the connection and command queue, cancels pending command completions, and audits allow/deny decisions. Reconnect creates a fresh queue; unknown or foreign agents return 404.
40: 
41: ### 4. Sensitive Data
42: - Secrets in .env only (never committed)
43: - API keys redacted in logs
44: - Tokens not returned to clients
45: - Credential files excluded from version control
46: - Authorization headers never logged (401 diagnostics record only path + header presence)
47: 
48: ### 5. Local dev convenience (single-user machines only)
49: - `TOLIK_DEV_AUTO_TOKEN=true` allows the same-machine WebUI to mint an owner
50:   session via `GET /auth/local-token` (explicit opt-in, default off).
51: - Endpoint answers only loopback/RFC1918 callers and 404s otherwise
52:   (indistinguishable from "no such endpoint" for outsiders).
53: - Core logs a startup warning while enabled. Never enable on shared/VPS hosts.
54: 
55: ### 5. Audit
56: - All important actions logged
57: - Structured audit events in PostgreSQL
58: - Actor, tool, arguments, result, timestamp
59: - Secrets never logged
60: - `audit_events` is append-only at both EF boundary and PostgreSQL trigger boundary
61: - `GET /audit` (authenticated, paginated) exposes the trail: Owner sees all,
62:   others only their own user-scoped events; auth endpoints (bootstrap, enroll,
63:   revoke) are audited ALLOW/DENY without logging codes, keys or tokens
64: 
65: ## .gitignore Key Rules
66: - .env files
67: - API keys, passwords, tokens
68: - Credential files
69: - Local development data
70: 
71: ## Bootstrap Flow
72: 1. First run → bootstrap challenge
73: 2. User provides bootstrap code
74: 3. Device registered with identity key
75: 4. Session credentials issued
76: 5. Revocation: `POST /auth/session/{id}/revoke`, `POST /auth/devices/{id}/revoke`
77:    (owner-scoped, audited; revoked devices fail all future authentication)
78: 
79: ## Dev-only secrets risk acceptance (01.10.2026)
80: - `src/TOLIK.Core.Host/appsettings.json` is tracked and holds dev-only local credentials (present since 17ec966), accepted for local dev only.
81: - MUST rotate PG password + bootstrap code and move to `.env`/user-secrets before any VPS deploy, repo sharing, or remote access.
82: - `.env` stays untracked/gitignored.

11: WHO ARE YOU? → ARE YOU AUTHENTICATED? → ARE YOU THE OWNER (or authorized role)?
12: → ARE YOU AUTHORIZED FOR THIS ACTION? → IS ADDITIONAL CONFIRMATION REQUIRED?
13: → EXECUTE → AUDIT
14: ```
15: 
16: Fail-closed at every arrow. The LLM never authorizes; only the Core
17: authorization layer decides.

19: ## Sensitivity categories (§16) → requirements
20: 
21: | Category | Tool risk levels | Authentication | Extra |
22: |---|---|---|---|
23: | LOW | `ReadOnly` (read/list/status) | session | none |
24: | MEDIUM | `LowRisk` (build/test/run/execute, sound) | session | none (rate-limited where annoying) |
25: | HIGH | `Modify`, `Destructive` (write, codex/opencode, security-path writes) | session, Owner/AuthorizedUser | explicit confirmation, single-use, 10-min TTL, bound to (task,step,capability,resource) |

28: Guest role: always denied. Voice confidence alone never authorizes
29: (`IdentityEvidence`: authenticated user id must equal requested user id).

content.text:
Now I have the normative matrix. Key facts:

1. Decision chain: WHO ARE YOU → AUTHENTICATED → OWNER or authorized role → AUTHORIZED FOR THIS ACTION → CONFIRMATION REQUIRED → EXECUTE → AUDIT.
2. HIGH category: Modify/Destructive requires "session, Owner/AuthorizedUser" + explicit confirmation.
3. CRITICAL: session + Owner + confirmation AND MFA — currently always Deny (MfaValid:false hardcoded at execute; gap C4).
4. Guest role: always denied.
5. Escalation rules raise risk (floor semantics).

So the current model's limitations with respect to "roles and ceilings":
- Roles are magic strings ("Owner"/"AuthorizedUser") compared at multiple scattered sites.
- There is no *ceiling*: the escalation rules define a *floor* (risk can only go up), but there's no per-role *maximum* risk. The doc's matrix says HIGH = Owner/AuthorizedUser, CRITICAL = Owner only. Currently, in `AuthorizationPolicy.Evaluate`, an AuthorizedUser with MfaValid+ConfirmationValid would be ALLOWED for Critical (line 119: `ToolRiskLevel.Critical => request.ConfirmationValid && request.MfaValid ? Allow : Deny`). Wait — but line 100 says `request.Risk == ToolRiskLevel.Critical && !request.MfaValid → Deny`. So an AuthorizedUser with MFA could get Critical allowed — that violates the normative matrix ("CRITICAL: session + Owner"). Hmm, but in practice MfaValid is hardcoded false at execute time, so Critical is always denied in production. Still, the policy function itself has this gap: the doc says CRITICAL requires Owner; the code doesn't enforce Owner for Critical — it enforces MFA for Critical, but a hypothetical AuthorizedUser+MFA would pass.

So "roles and authorization ceilings" should mean:
1. **Roles**: a formal role model in code — an `AuthorizationRole`/`IdentityRole` mapping with explicit semantics: Guest (deny all), AuthorizedUser (up to some ceiling), Owner (up to Critical). Replace scattered magic strings with a single role policy.
2. **Authorization ceilings**: a per-role maximum risk level (ceiling) — the escalation rules are the floor, the ceiling is the maximum. Effective risk = max(declared, escalated) must be ≤ role ceiling, else Deny (fail closed). This also fixes the matrix compliance: CRITICAL requires Owner (ceiling of AuthorizedUser = Destructive), HIGH (Modify/Destructive) allows Owner/AuthorizedUser.

This is the minimal coherent implementation:
- In `TOLIK.Contracts`: there's already `IdentityRole` enum (Guest, AuthorizedUser, Owner). Could add a `RoleCeiling`/`AuthorizationCeiling` static class mapping IdentityRole → max ToolRiskLevel. But wait — `SessionPrincipal.Role` is a string, not the enum. The policy takes the string. Converting string → enum: "Owner" → IdentityRole.Owner, "AuthorizedUser" → IdentityRole.AuthorizedUser, "Guest" → IdentityRole.Guest. Any other/unknown string → deny (fail closed).

Where to put the ceiling? Options:
a) `TOLIK.Contracts` — `IdentityAuthorization` static class already exists in IdentityEvidence.cs (with IsAuthorized). Add role ceiling mapping there.
b) `TOLIK.Infrastructure.Authorization` — `AuthorizationPolicy` already there.

The ceiling is a policy decision used by `AuthorizationPolicy.Evaluate` in Infrastructure. But the role enum is in Contracts. The mapping from role string to ceiling could live in Infrastructure.Authorization as a `RoleCeilings` static class, e.g.:

```csharp
public static class RoleCeilings
{
    public static ToolRiskLevel? CeilingFor(string? role) => role switch
    {
        "Owner" => ToolRiskLevel.Critical,
        "AuthorizedUser" => ToolRiskLevel.Destructive,
        _ => null // unknown/guest/unset roles have no ceiling = deny everything
    };
}
```

Hmm wait — actually "Guest" should also be denied. Currently the policy denies everything except Owner/AuthorizedUser. With ceilings: Guest → ceiling = ReadOnly? or deny? The doc says "Guest role: always denied." So Guest → deny all (null ceiling → deny).

But wait — there's a subtlety: ceiling for AuthorizedUser = Destructive means an AuthorizedUser can do Destructive ops with confirmation. The current matrix says HIGH = Owner/AuthorizedUser + confirmation. So AuthorizedUser ceiling should be Destructive (allows Modify and Destructive), Critical requires Owner. That matches the normative matrix exactly. 

Also, ceiling enforcement should apply to the *effective* risk (max(declared, escalated)) — fail closed: if effective risk > ceiling → Deny (not ConfirmationRequired, since no amount of confirmation can raise a ceiling).

Now, where exactly to integrate:
- `AuthorizationPolicy.Evaluate`: add ceiling check in the deny chain: if `RoleCeilings.CeilingFor(request.Principal.Role)` is null → Deny; if effectiveRisk > ceiling → Deny.

This single change:
- Replaces the scattered magic-string role check inside the policy with a single role policy (still uses the string, but through one function).
- Enforces CRITICAL = Owner only (fixes the matrix violation where AuthorizedUser+MFA could pass Critical).
- Adds the ceiling concept complementary to escalation floors.
- Fail closed: unknown roles, Guest, empty role → Deny.
- No privilege escalation: Owner ceiling = Critical preserves existing Owner behavior (Critical requires MFA + confirmation — unchanged). AuthorizedUser behavior: currently could reach Critical with MFA — but MFA is hardcoded false at execute, so in production AuthorizedUser could reach Destructive (Modify/Destructive with confirmation) — ceiling = Destructive preserves that. Wait, is that right? Let me check: current production path for AuthorizedUser with Modify/Destructive: `ToolRiskLevel.Modify => ConfirmationValid ? Allow : ConfirmationRequired`. Yes. And Critical: MfaValid=false hardcoded → Deny. So AuthorizedUser effective max in production = Destructive. Ceiling = Destructive. 

Also, there's `Program.cs:764` — confirmation approve requires Owner (magic string). And `Program.cs:1015` — audit view: Owner sees all. Should I centralize those too? The task says "roles and authorization ceilings" — the minimal coherent implementation. Centralizing role checks into a single role-policy static class would prevent drift. But minimal: maybe add helper methods like `AuthorizationRoles.IsOwner(role)`? Hmm.

Wait, let me also check the confirmation approve endpoint: it requires Owner. With ceilings, should approve also enforce the ceiling? The approval is for a specific confirmation with EffectiveRisk. An AuthorizedUser cannot approve (owner_role_required). That's already consistent with the matrix.

Now let me finalize the design. Let me summarize my analysis:

## Current authorization model

1. **Identity**: `IdentityService` — bootstrap code → device challenge (P256 signature) → owner enrollment (single-use, serializable tx) → session tokens (SHA-256 hashed, sliding expiration). MFA: TOTP enrollment/verification on devices. `AuthenticateAsync` returns `SessionPrincipal(UserId, DeviceId, SessionId, Role)` — Role is a DB string ("Owner").

2. **Authorization**: `AuthorizationPolicy.Evaluate(AuthorizationRequest)` — deterministic, fail-closed:
   - Deny chain: policy unavailable, null principal, invalid session/device/agent/task scope, capability not granted, role must be exactly "Owner" or "AuthorizedUser" (magic strings), Critical requires MFA, resource/allowedResource must be non-empty and equal, authorization expiry, confirmation consumed/expired.
   - Effective risk = max(declared, escalated via ToolEscalation rules).
   - Switch: ReadOnly/LowRisk → Allow; Modify/Destructive → confirmation ? Allow : ConfirmationRequired; Critical → confirmation && MFA ? Allow : Deny.

3. **Confirmation**: `ConfirmationStore` — single-use, SHA-256-bound to (task, step, capability, resource), 10-min TTL. Approve requires Owner (Program.cs:764) and Critical approvals hard-refused (strong_auth_required). MFA at execute is hardcoded false (gap C4 — Critical always Deny in production).

4. **Transport**: `AgentTransportAuthorization` — registration validation, advertised capability, forbidden-argument denylist, then `AuthorizationPolicy` (confirmation always false).

5. **Audit**: `AuditWriter` — hash-chained (SHA-256 chain, pg advisory lock), redacted, structured. Decisions audited at endpoints. UnauthorizedAccessException at execute → task failed, 403 (no dedicated audit row at that exact point, but the task lifecycle records the failure; hmm, actually — wait, let me double check the UnauthorizedAccessException catch: lines 948-954 — no audit write. Hmm. But is the denial audited anywhere? The dispatch throws before execution; the catch doesn't audit. That's an existing audit gap for capability denials at execute time... but not my scope to change (audit guarantees must remain intact — I must not weaken; adding an audit row would strengthen but it's out of scope; actually wait, should I? The task says "Existing audit guarantees must remain intact" — I preserve them. Adding ceiling-denial audit would be nice but the task says smallest coherent implementation. The dispatch denial throw message contains the reason; the task is marked Failed. I'll leave the audit flow untouched.)

6. **Roles**: magic strings "Owner"/"AuthorizedUser" in AuthorizationPolicy; "Owner" checks in Program.cs (confirmation approve :764, audit view :1015); DB `TolikUser.Role` string (default "Owner"); `IdentityRole` enum in Contracts (Guest, AuthorizedUser, Owner) used by wire protocol RequesterIdentity.

## Limitations (w.r.t. roles/ceilings)

1. Roles are magic strings scattered across 3 files — no single role model.
2. No risk ceiling: escalation defines a floor (risk only goes up), but nothing caps what a role may reach. The policy's role gate ("Owner"||"AuthorizedUser") makes no distinction between the two roles — an AuthorizedUser with MFA could reach Critical, violating the normative matrix ("CRITICAL: session + Owner").
3. The reference (interface/policy.js, backlog TODO #65) defines ROLE_RISK_CEILING — Guest/TrustedGuest/Family/Owner with ceilings; the .NET side lacks this entirely.

Hmm, but there's a running production Core (tolik-core-1) connected to the same postgres on 5432. The integration tests create separate `tolik_test_*` databases on the same server — isolated per test. That's how the previous session ran them (154 green). OK.

Now let me get back to the design work. I have all the information I need. Let me finalize:

## Design (final)

**Concept — "roles and authorization ceilings"** (from backlog TODO line 65 in docs/INTERFACE-ANALYSIS.md + reference interface/policy.js ROLE_RISK_CEILING + normative docs/authorization.md):
- A role's **ceiling** is the maximum **effective risk** (max(declared, escalated)) that role may ever be authorized for.
- Escalation (ToolEscalation) raises risk toward the ceiling (floor semantics); the ceiling can never be raised by confirmation or MFA — ceiling-exceeded → Deny (fail closed).
- Role semantics aligned to the normative matrix: Guest → nothing (always denied); AuthorizedUser → ceiling Destructive (HIGH category: Modify/Destructive with confirmation; CRITICAL denied — "session + Owner"); Owner → ceiling Critical (unchanged production behavior).
- Unknown/unresolvable role strings → fail closed (deny everything).

**Changes:**

1. **`src/TOLIK.Infrastructure/Authorization/AuthorizationRoles.cs`** (new) — the role model:
   - Role name constants (Owner, AuthorizedUser, Guest) — the DB role strings in one place.
   - `TryResolve(string?, out IdentityRole)` — fail-closed string→enum resolution.
   - `CeilingFor(IdentityRole)` → `ToolRiskLevel?` — the ROLE_RISK_CEILING table.
   - `IsOwner(string?)` — owner-only gate for the scattered endpoint checks.

2. **`src/TOLIK.Infrastructure/Authorization/AuthorizationPolicy.cs`** (edit):
   - Replace the magic-string role check in the deny chain with the role resolution (`IsKnown` — hmm, or keep it simple).
   - Add the ceiling check after effective-risk computation: `ceiling is null || effectiveRisk > ceiling → Deny`.

Let me think once more about the exact policy shape. Current deny chain includes:
```
string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.Principal.Role) ||
!string.Equals(request.Principal.Role, "Owner", ...) &&
!string.Equals(request.Principal.Role, "AuthorizedUser", ...) ||
```

Minimal edit that keeps the deny chain semantics: replace those two lines with the ceiling-based gate. But the ceiling gate needs the effective risk... The cleanest minimal approach:

Option 1 (two gates):
- Deny chain: `!AuthorizationRoles.IsAuthorizedRole(request.Principal.Role)` where IsAuthorizedRole = TryResolve (Guest resolves but ceiling denies later)... hmm, this splits "Guest denied" across two places, which is less clear.

Option 2 (single ceiling gate after effective risk):
- Remove the role check from the deny chain entirely; after computing effectiveRisk:
```csharp
var ceiling = AuthorizationRoles.CeilingFor(request.Principal.Role);  // Principal non-null here (deny chain checked)
if (ceiling is null || effectiveRisk > ceiling) return AuthorizationDecision.Deny;
```
- One gate, one concept. Guest/unknown/empty → null ceiling → Deny. ✓
- The deny chain still checks `request.Risk == Critical && !MfaValid` (declared-risk critical) — preserved.
- Ceiling check sits exactly where the reference puts it: after escalation, before confirmation evaluation. ✓

I prefer Option 2 — it's the smallest coherent change: the role gate moves into the ceiling concept (one place), everything else preserved.

Wait, one consideration: in Option 2, for a request with an INVALID role and ReadOnly risk, evaluation order changes (no early deny) but the decision is the same Deny. Tests pass. And `request.Principal.Role` null-conditional — Principal is null-checked in the deny chain first, so by the time we reach the ceiling check, Principal is non-null. But CeilingFor(string?) accepts null anyway.

3. **`src/TOLIK.Core.Host/Program.cs`** (edit, 2 sites):
   - Line 764: `if (!string.Equals(principal.Role, "Owner", StringComparison.Ordinal))` → `if (!AuthorizationRoles.IsOwner(principal.Role))`.
   - Line 1015: same → `if (AuthorizationRoles.IsOwner(principal.Role))`.
   - Behavior identical (ordinal "Owner" comparison); role semantics now defined in ONE place.
   
   Hmm — wait. Should the confirmation-approve endpoint's owner gate also enforce the ceiling? E.g., should approving a confirmation whose EffectiveRisk exceeds the approver's ceiling be denied? The approve endpoint requires Owner (ceiling Critical — max possible), so any confirmation's effective risk ≤ Critical = ceiling. No-op. Skip.

   Hmm — but hold on, is there a subtlety with the ceiling on the approve path? `PendingConfirmation.RequiresMfa` → EffectiveRisk == Critical → approve hard-refused (strong_auth_required) — MFA approval happens through /mfa/verify... which sets MfaLastVerifiedAt but how does that flow into AuthorizationPolicy? It doesn't — MfaValid is hardcoded false at execute. So Critical is always denied at execute (gap C4, documented, out of scope — "Treat as denied until the MFA chain is closed").

4. **Audit of ceiling denials**: The policy returns only an enum. The dispatch path's denial throw already includes capability + effective risk. I'll extend the throw message to include the role ceiling, so the task event stream and task failure record carry the reason. Hmm — actually, let me reconsider. The current message: `$"capability_denied:{capability};risk={effectiveRisk}"`. With ceilings, there are two deny causes: (a) ceiling exceeded, (b) the existing deny chain. Both land in the same throw. Adding `;ceiling={ceiling}` to the message is informative and harmless. Hmm, but wait — the message is asserted anywhere? Let me search for "capability_denied" in tests.

Actually — a cleaner approach for audit: since the policy is a pure function, I could add an optional reason out-parameter... no, that changes the signature used in 3 places + tests. Minimal: include the ceiling in the dispatch denial message. Let me check test references to capability_denied first.

5. **Documentation updates**:
   - `docs/authorization.md`: add the role ceiling table (normative) — roles, ceilings, fail-closed semantics; update the CRITICAL row note.
   - `docs/INTERFACE-ANALYSIS.md` line 65: mark `[x]` IMPLEMENTED with the pattern used by lines 64/66 (description + tests count + date).
   - `docs/SECURITY.md` §2: maybe add a line about role ceilings. Minimal — the matrix reference is already there; I'll add the ceilings to authorization.md and a short line in SECURITY.md.

6. **Tests** (add to `tests/TOLIK.Foundation.Tests/AuthorizationTests.cs` — new test class `RoleCeilingTests` or extend existing `AuthorizationPolicyTests`):
   - `Owner_ceiling_is_Critical`: ceiling mapping table (Owner→Critical, AuthorizedUser→Destructive, Guest→null).
   - `TryResolve_is_fail_closed`: "Owner"→Owner, "AuthorizedUser"→AuthorizedUser, "Guest"→Guest, "Superuser"/""/null/false (default)→false.
   - `Unknown_role_denies_even_read_only`: policy deny for "Superuser", "", null principal role.
   - `Guest_denies_everything`: Guest principal + ReadOnly → Deny (normative: Guest always denied).
   - `AuthorizedUser_ceiling_blocks_critical_even_with_mfa_and_confirmation`: AuthorizedUser + Critical + MfaValid=true + ConfirmationValid=true → Deny (normative CRITICAL: session + Owner). This is the key negative/privilege-escalation test.
   - `AuthorizedUser_within_ceiling_allows_modify_and_destructive_with_confirmation`: AuthorizedUser + Modify/Destructive + confirmation → Allow (HIGH category preserved).
   - `Ceiling_applies_to_effective_risk_after_escalation`: AuthorizedUser + WriteFile on security-critical source (escalates to Critical > Destructive ceiling) → Deny even with confirmation; Owner same request → Allow with confirmation+MFA (unchanged).
   - `Ceiling_does_not_escalate_below_ceiling`: AuthorizedUser + WriteFile security-configuration (escalates to Destructive == ceiling) → ConfirmationRequired/Allow-with-confirmation (boundary: ceiling is inclusive).
   - `Transport_authorization_inherits_ceilings`: AgentTransportAuthorization with AuthorizedUser + WriteFile Critical-effective → Deny; Owner + same → Deny (MFA unavailable in transport — existing fail-closed)... hmm wait, for Owner transport + Critical-effective: switch Critical → ConfirmationValid(false) && MfaValid(false) → Deny. So both deny. Better transport test: AuthorizedUser + RunCodex (Modify effective ≤ ceiling) → ConfirmationRequired (same as today). Hmm, what distinguishes ceiling in transport? A capability whose effective risk exceeds the AuthorizedUser ceiling but is not Critical-declared: WriteFile on security-critical source → effective Critical. For AuthorizedUser: ceiling Destructive < Critical → **Deny** (with ceilings) — but WITHOUT ceilings, the old policy would give: line 100 (declared Risk==Critical? No, declared Modify) → switch Critical → ConfirmationValid(false)&&MfaValid(false) → Deny. Same Deny! Hmm. So for transport, the ceiling produces the same Deny as the existing MFA gate. OK — the transport test then verifies ceilings don't accidentally ALLOW something (regression guard).
   
   Hmm wait, what about a ceiling DENY in transport that would previously NOT be denied? For that I need effective risk ≤ Critical (so the old MFA gate doesn't fire) but > ceiling. Ceiling(AuthorizedUser)=Destructive. Effective > Destructive and ≤ Critical means effective == Critical. But effective==Critical fires the old MFA gate (line 100 only for declared Critical; the switch fires for effective Critical → Deny without MFA). So for AuthorizedUser, ceiling-deny and existing-MFA-deny coincide. For Guest: ceiling null → everything denied — previously Guest was denied by the role check. Also coincides. So in the current policy, ceilings ADD no new denies for transport... they add a new deny ONLY for AuthorizedUser+MFA+Critical (which requires MfaValid=true — only reachable in the policy function, not in transport where ConfirmationValid=false and MfaValid=false... wait, MfaValid defaults false in the transport call, so line 119's Allow branch never fires).

   Hmm — so wait, where does the ceiling actually ADD a new denial in production?
   
   Production paths:
   a) `/tasks` POST: `AuthorizationPolicy.Evaluate(principal, RunBuild, LowRisk, "task", "task", false)` — Owner or AuthorizedUser → LowRisk ≤ both ceilings → Allow. No change.
   b) `DispatchGuardedAsync`: declared risk from server, confirmation consumed, MfaValid=false. For Owner: unchanged. For AuthorizedUser: effective Critical (security-source write) → old: switch Critical → Deny (no MFA); new: ceiling Destructive < Critical → Deny. Same outcome. For AuthorizedUser: effective Destructive (security-config write) → old: confirmation → Allow/ConfirmationRequired; new: ceiling Destructive — inclusive → same. No change.
   c) Transport: as analyzed — no new denies, no new allows.
   
   So in production TODAY (only Owner exists), ceilings change NOTHING observable. The capability is forward-looking: it makes roles meaningful the moment a second role (AuthorizedUser) can be minted, and it closes the latent policy-level escalation (AuthorizedUser+MFA→Critical) that the normative matrix forbids.

   Hmm — wait, is that really the "next missing capability"? Let me re-read the backlog TODO: "Roles: Guest/TrustedGuest/Family/Owner + risk ceilings в AuthorizationPolicy". Yes — this is exactly it: bring the role/ceiling model into AuthorizationPolicy. The production impact being zero today is CORRECT and desirable: it's a security capability that must not change existing guarantees; it becomes load-bearing when non-Owner roles exist.

   Hmm, but hold on. Let me reconsider whether the ceiling for AuthorizedUser should be Destructive or Modify, because that's the one real semantic decision. Evidence:
   - Normative matrix HIGH row: "Modify, Destructive (write, codex/opencode, security-path writes) | session, Owner/AuthorizedUser | explicit confirmation" — AuthorizedUser allowed for Modify AND Destructive.
   - CRITICAL row: "session + Owner".
   - So AuthorizedUser ceiling = Destructive. ✓ This is what the normative doc says. I'll document it in authorization.md.

   And the reference's Family=Modify — the reference's role set differs (Family < TrustedGuest? no: TrustedGuest < Family). AuthorizedUser ≈ which reference role? The .NET AuthorizedUser sits between Guest and Owner — closest to Family. But the .NET normative matrix grants AuthorizedUser Destructive. Since docs/authorization.md is "Single source of truth for who may do what" for the C# system, ceiling(AuthorizedUser)=Destructive. I'll note the mapping divergence in the docs (same pattern as the README divergence note in INTERFACE-ANALYSIS.md).

Now — one more design question: where should the ceiling table live — Infrastructure.Authorization or Contracts? 

Consideration: `IdentityRole` and `ToolRiskLevel` are in Contracts. The ceiling table maps IdentityRole → ToolRiskLevel — pure contract-level types. The reference has it in policy.js (the policy layer). The existing C# pattern: `CommandArgumentPolicy` (pure contract policy) lives in Contracts and is shared by validation + transport authorization. A ceiling table in Contracts would similarly be reusable by any layer... but the enforcement is Infrastructure-only today.

Hmm. The backlog TODO says "в AuthorizationPolicy" (in AuthorizationPolicy). So the ceiling goes into the authorization policy layer = `TOLIK.Infrastructure.Authorization`. But `SessionPrincipal` is in Infrastructure.Identity and `AuthorizationRequest` is in Infrastructure.Authorization — the ceiling table operating on the principal's role string belongs there. 

But hmm — what about `IdentityRole` resolution? `TryResolve` maps DB strings to the contract enum. If I put the whole role model in Infrastructure.Authorization, it references TOLIK.Contracts (fine).

Hmm, wait — actually, let me reconsider putting the ceiling table in Contracts next to `IdentityAuthorization` (IdentityEvidence.cs). The `IdentityAuthorization.IsAuthorized` static is already there — a policy function in Contracts. The ceiling table is a natural sibling: `RoleCeilings.CeilingFor(IdentityRole)`. Then Infrastructure.Authorization's policy consumes it. Hmm.

Deciding factor: the backlog TODO says "в AuthorizationPolicy" — the policy layer. Also AGENTS.md §33: contracts stay technology-agnostic — a ceiling table IS technology-agnostic (pure enums). But the string→role resolution (DB role strings) is Infrastructure. 

I'll put the **ceiling table + role constants + TryResolve + IsOwner in `TOLIK.Infrastructure.Authorization`** (new file `AuthorizationRoles.cs`), because:
1. The backlog TODO targets AuthorizationPolicy.
2. The enforcement (the only consumer) is Infrastructure.Authorization.
3. It keeps Contracts unchanged (no wire-contract changes — safest).
4. The string constants match the DB role strings (Infrastructure persistence concern).

Hmm, wait — but should I extend the `IdentityRole` enum with TrustedGuest/Family? I decided against it (no enrollment path; contract change; normative matrix doesn't cover them). The backlog TODO names them though... Let me think about what "smallest coherent implementation" means here ONE more time.

The capability = "roles and authorization ceilings". The ESSENCE: role-based risk ceilings in the authorization policy. The role SET: the existing .NET role set (Guest/AuthorizedUser/Owner) covers all roles that can exist in the system today. TrustedGuest/Family exist only in the reference prototype with no .NET enrollment path. Adding them to the ceiling table keyed on the ENUM would require enum extension. BUT — I could define the ceiling table over the enum AND note that TrustedGuest/Family arrive with enrollment. OR define ceilings keyed on the string role and include TrustedGuest/Family mappings that are inert...

Hmm. Actually — you know what, let me look at this from the fail-closed angle: `TryResolve` maps strings → enum. If a future enrollment path mints "TrustedGuest" (a string), TryResolve returns false → deny. Fail closed. ✓. When TrustedGuest enrollment lands, TryResolve and CeilingFor get extended. That's the incremental path (§53, §57.16: smallest change that correctly solves the problem).

Decision: implement over the existing 3-role set; document TrustedGuest/Family as future work aligned with the reference. The backlog TODO gets marked implemented for the ceiling mechanism with a note. Hmm... 

Hmm, wait. Actually, let me reconsider ONE more time whether to include TrustedGuest/Family in the enum. 

Arguments FOR including them now:
- The backlog TODO explicitly names them.
- AGENTS.md SECURITY §18: "Supported identity states should include: UNKNOWN GUEST TRUSTED_GUEST FAMILY OWNER".
- The reference defines ceilings for them.
- Adding enum values is backward-compatible on the wire (allowIntegerValues:false, names unchanged for existing values).

Arguments AGAINST:
- No enrollment path → they cannot be minted → the mappings are inert (dead code until enrollment lands).
- The normative matrix (single source of truth) doesn't assign them permissions — I'd have to invent ceilings (from the reference: TrustedGuest=LowRisk, Family=Modify) — which the matrix doesn't endorse.
- The task: "smallest coherent implementation"; "Do not invent a parallel authorization system".
- RequesterIdentity.Role at the wire boundary would ACCEPT "family"/"trustedGuest" — expanding what untrusted clients can send. The authorization policy would still deny (no principal role mapping → deny), but the contract boundary accepting new values is a (tiny) widening.

Hmm. The AGENTS.md says "should include" (future), not "must include now". The normative matrix governs. I'll go WITHOUT extending the enum, and note it in the report + docs. The ceiling mechanism itself (the actual capability) is fully implemented.

Hmm, hold on, wait. Let me reconsider the whole framing once more. Let me re-read the task statement:

"Your task is to implement the next missing authorization/security capability in the existing system: roles and authorization ceilings."

"IMPORTANT: First inspect the current authorization architecture, security documentation, tests, DTOs/contracts, middleware/services and audit flow. Determine what 'roles and ceilings' should mean from the existing code and documentation."

From the existing code and documentation:
- interface/policy.js: ROLE_ORDER, ROLE_RISK_CEILING, CAPABILITY_MIN_ROLE — roles with risk ceilings.
- docs/INTERFACE-ANALYSIS.md line 65: backlog TODO "Roles: Guest/TrustedGuest/Family/Owner + risk ceilings в AuthorizationPolicy".
- docs/authorization.md (normative): role distinctions Guest=denied, HIGH=Owner/AuthorizedUser, CRITICAL=Owner.

So "roles and ceilings" = port the ceiling model into AuthorizationPolicy with role semantics matching the normative matrix. ✓ My design does this.

"Determine ... the smallest coherent implementation that fits the existing architecture." ✓

OK. Now let me also double-check: is there maybe an existing partial "ceiling" implementation somewhere I missed? Let me grep for "ceiling" and "Ceiling" in src.
All the context is gathered. Let me do a final check for any existing ceiling references in src, and check how `capability_denied` is referenced in tests.
